summary: This page covers stick welding troubleshooting topics including slag coating, porosity, crooked/wavy bead, excessive spatter, and burn-through, with causes and solutions for each defect.
text_content:
Stick Weld–Coat of Slag Over Weld
TOP VIEW
PARTIALLY CHIPPED AWAY TO SHOW WELD
Slag is a necessary part of a stick weld. It shields the weld from impurities. Clean off the slag with the Chipping Hammer and Wire Brush after welding.

Stick Weld–Porosity — Small cavities or holes in the bead.
POSSIBLE CAUSES AND SOLUTIONS
TOP VIEW
1. Dirty workpiece or fill material:
Clean workpiece down to bare metal.
Make certain that fill material and Electrode are clean and free from oil, coatings, and other residues.
2. Inconsistent welding speed:
Maintain steady weld speed.

Stick Weld–Crooked/Wavy Bead
POSSIBLE CAUSES AND SOLUTIONS
TOP VIEW
1. Inaccurate welding:
Use two hands or rest hand on steady surface.
2. Inconsistent welding speed:
Maintain steady weld speed.

Stick Weld–Excessive Spatter
POSSIBLE CAUSES AND SOLUTIONS
TOP VIEW
Fine spatter is normal. Spatter that is grainy and large is a problem.
Dirty workpiece or fill material:
Clean workpiece down to bare metal.
Make certain that fill material and Electrode are clean and free from oil, coatings, and other residues.

Stick Weld–Burn-Through — Base material melts away, leaving a hole in the weld.
POSSIBLE CAUSES AND SOLUTIONS
TOP VIEW
1. Workpiece overheating:
Reduce current.
2. Welding speed too slow:
Increase welding speed and ensure that welding speed is kept steady.
3. Excessive material at weld:
Reduce amount of fill material.

key_facts: Slag is a necessary part of a stick weld and shields the weld from impurities
Slag must be cleaned off with a Chipping Hammer and Wire Brush after welding
Porosity in stick welding is defined as small cavities or holes in the bead
Porosity can be caused by a dirty workpiece or fill material
Porosity can be caused by inconsistent welding speed
To fix porosity from dirty materials: clean workpiece down to bare metal and ensure electrode and fill material are free from oil, coatings, and other residues
Crooked/wavy bead can be caused by inaccurate welding technique
Crooked/wavy bead solution: use two hands or rest hand on a steady surface
Inconsistent welding speed causes both porosity and crooked/wavy bead
Fine spatter is normal in stick welding; grainy and large spatter is a problem
Excessive spatter is caused by dirty workpiece or fill material
Burn-through is defined as base material melting away, leaving a hole in the weld
Burn-through cause 1: workpiece overheating – solution is to reduce current
Burn-through cause 2: welding speed too slow – solution is to increase and maintain steady welding speed
Burn-through cause 3: excessive material at weld – solution is to reduce amount of fill material
